newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq pares some losses, major techs still weak.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq pares some losses, major techs still weak.

text.p: Intel Corp and other Nasdaq shares recovered some of their initial losses as bargain-hunters moved in following an early selloff, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 23.06 points, or 1.64 percent, at 1379.98, compared to a drop of about 47 points at the opening.

Intel, which warned early today that its second quarter results will fall short of expectations, was down 13-1/164 to 150-3/4 at 1107 EDT/1507 GMT. The stock opened at 142-1/2, down from Thursday's close at 163-49/64.

"There was an initial panic as people said, 'Intel -- a major bellwether -- oh my God.' But then they looked at the news a little more and saw that gross margins are going to be about 60 percent instead of 64 percent. That's just a tempest in a teapot," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president at Unterberg Harris.
Another trader said, "Earnings warnings are never good. But there are some portfolio managers out there eager to buy techs a lot cheaper than they could yesterday."
Despite the slight recovery, the major technology issues were still suffering in late-morning trading.
Dell Computer Corp was off 1/2 to 109-7/8 but up from its morning low of 99-1/2. Microsoft Corp was down 1-3/8 to 124-1/2, recovering from a low of 117-1/2 at the opening bell.
Of the 25 most active Nasdaq issues, only Cyrix Corp showed major gains, rising 2-7/8 to 24-7/8.
Earlier today Cyrix introduced its latest challenge to Intel's domination of the personal computer chip industry with a processor that it said competes with Intel's Pentium II at half the price.
Declining issues outnumbered gainers by two to one, with 2,186 losers compared to 1,081 gainers on volume of 264 million shares.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index was down 8.90 points, or 2.79 percent, at 310.14. The Morgan Stanley High Tech index was off 4.93 points, or 1.15 percent, at 424.88.
